construct: DGAT1 is an acyl-CoA:diacylglycerol acyltransferase highly expressed in human enterocytes that catalyzes the final step of triglyceride synthesis by adding a fatty acyl-CoA to diacylglycerol. Biallelic DGAT1 loss can cause severe early-onset diarrhea and protein-losing enteropathy.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Severe infantile diarrhea/protein-losing enteropathy with biallelic DGAT1 loss identifies failure of the final triglyceride-synthesis step: acyl-CoA addition to diacylglycerol.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Pancreatic lipase hydrolyzes luminal triglyceride, ACAT esterifies cholesterol, MTTP lipidates apoB particles, and beta-oxidation degrades fatty acyl-CoA; none is the DGAT1 reaction.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Gene identity and reaction specificity make the keyed biochemical step uniquely correct.
